collection.credit:
ISOLA — BEYOND THE HORIZON: THE WORLD WE IMAGINE
A NEW, SEPARATE COMPANION EVENT ANTHOLOGY FOR VIRTUAL VILLAGERS 1–5

collection.description: While sharing roasted fruit, a child asks whether families beyond the ocean wake up hungry and argue about breakfast too.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: While sharing roasted fruit, a child asks whether families beyond the ocean wake up hungry and argue about breakfast too.

a1.name: Outcome A1
a1.text: The children invent a distant family who burns their morning bread and laughs; the cook admits that sounds entirely plausible.

a2.name: Outcome A2
a2.text: An elder remembers that even neighboring households eat differently; the group sketches many possible breakfasts instead of one.

b1.name: Outcome B1
b1.text: A gardener describes grains, roots, and creatures they have never seen; everyone grows hungry during the discussion.

b2.name: Outcome B2
b2.text: The wild guesses turn into an argument over what can safely be eaten; a healer reminds them that novelty is not proof of nourishment.

c1.name: Outcome C1
c1.text: A parent suggests that sharing food might comfort people anywhere, whatever is on the plate.

text_only.reason: food talked about or imagined; the village's stores do not change

c2.name: Outcome C2
c2.text: A solitary villager says some people may eat alone by preference or necessity; the table falls thoughtfully quiet.
